children: Demand for U.S. durable goods was unchanged in August, according to data published by the Commerce Department.
Total orders for durable goods--which comprise goods meant to last three years or more-decreased $0.1 billion in August to $338.6 billion, following a 0.9% July increase.
Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had expected a decrease of 0.3%.
Transportation equipment, down three of the last four months, drove the decrease, falling 0.6%. Excluding defense, new orders increased 0.1%.

Durable Goods Orders Were Unchanged in August
Demand for U.S. durable goods was unchanged in August, according to data published by the Commerce Department.
Total orders for durable goods--which comprise goods meant to last three years or more-decreased $0.1 billion in August to $338.6 billion, following a 0.9% July increase.
Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had expected a decrease of 0.3%.
Transportation equipment, down three of the last four months, drove the decrease, falling 0.6%. Excluding defense, new orders increased 0.1%.
